case: PostgreSQL timestamptz[] workbook re-import through Calc under a non-UTC source session
contract: The workbook is generated from a PostgreSQL transaction with TimeZone America/New_York; PostgreSQL's independent array text and array_to_json oracles show the two distinct fall-back offsets.
BookiE decodes the timestamptz[] result to canonical UTC array text, which is stored as a shared-string XLSX cell.
Calc opens source.xlsx, saves calc-roundtrip.ods, reopens it and saves calc-roundtrip.xlsx; both retain the exact canonical UTC array text, string cell type, and no formula.
The checker pins both repeated-hour UTC instants, the BC instant, infinities and SQL NULL in the preserved text.

native_export_test.command: rtk proxy env BOOKIEE_XLSX_REIMPORT_ARTIFACT=<evidence-dir>/source.xlsx cargo test --locked -p tablepro-driver-postgres --test integration array_contract::value_contract_timestamptz_array_file_exports_preserve_instants_under_non_utc_session -- --include-ignored --exact --test-threads=1

steps: Install libreoffice-calc 4:26.8.0.3-2 in the pinned Debian container.
Open source.xlsx in Calc and save calc-roundtrip.ods.
Open calc-roundtrip.ods in Calc and save calc-roundtrip.xlsx.

consumer_assertions.method: Python standard-library ZIP/XML checks exact A2 text in source and re-saved XLSX/ODS, requires string cell kinds and rejects formulas.
consumer_assertions.result: Canonical UTC array text and both repeated-hour instants preserved in all three workbooks.

remaining: Other spreadsheet applications, temporal-array session combinations and the broader B3 matrix remain open.
